root_cause_label: Incorrect Jaxley Channel Implementation Without Validation
one_sentence_failure_summary: After discovering jaxley was unimportable in steps 5-8, the agent nonetheless wrote add_channels() using hallucinated channel class names (jx.channels.Na/K/Ca/KCa and string-based insert), then spent the remaining steps on static syntax checks and completion claims without ever correcting the fundamentally wrong API usage.
t_err_evidence: Step 9: Agent writes jaxley_conversion.py using jx.channels.Leak(), jx.channels.Na(), jx.channels.K(), jx.channels.Ca(), jx.channels.KCa() — channel class names that do not exist in the actual Jaxley library — despite having confirmed in steps 5-8 that jaxley cannot even be imported for verification. This is the decisive wrong action based on hallucinated API knowledge.
t_commit_evidence: Step 9: Once the wrong channel API implementation is committed to file, all subsequent steps (12: switch to string-based insert which is also wrong, 13-16: static syntax checks, 17-18: completion claims) preserve the same fundamental error. The agent never obtains access to jaxley to verify or correct the channel names, locking in failure.
t_surface_evidence: Step 11: Running python test_jaxley_conversion.py produces ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'jaxley', which is the first observable runtime failure signal (though it reveals the missing dependency, not the wrong channel API directly).
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked knowledge of Jaxley's actual channel API. It invented plausible-sounding but non-existent channel classes (jx.channels.Na, jx.channels.K, jx.channels.Ca, jx.channels.KCa, jx.channels.Leak) and could not verify them because jaxley was not installed in the execution environment. The inability to import jaxley in steps 5-8 should have prompted the agent to find alternative API documentation, but instead it proceeded on fabricated assumptions.
forewarning_evidence: Step 5: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'jaxley' when attempting to introspect available channels. Step 8: pip list | grep -i jax returns empty output (returncode 1), confirming jaxley is not installed. Both signals appear before step 9 where the wrong implementation is committed.
